title: Digest downloads can escape the intended Epilogue directory
reasoning: The repository writes response bytes to File(documentsDir, filename/outputFilename) without validating that the resolved path remains inside the Epilogue download directory. If a server-provided digest filename, or a caller-derived output name, contains path traversal or an absolute path, the write can target a sibling or parent app-controlled location instead of the intended directory.
reproduction: Have the Ghostwriter server return a digest filename like ../unexpected.epub, then trigger a sync path that calls downloadDigest(filename). The repository resolves and writes that path without rejecting it.
recommendation: Accept only safe basenames for downloaded artifacts, reject names containing path separators, absolute paths, or traversal segments, and verify the canonical output path starts with the canonical Epilogue directory before writing.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The linked SharedGhostwriterAdapter test only verifies raw download bytes for a normal filename; no repository test covers local path resolution or unsafe filenames.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a GhostwriterRepository download test with filenames such as ../escape.epub and /tmp/escape.epub and assert the method rejects them without creating files outside the Epilogue directory.
minimumFixScope: Add filename sanitization/canonical-path validation in GhostwriterRepository downloadDigest and downloadDigestById, then cover both call paths with tests.

history.reasoning: The original evidence paths still exist, but the vulnerable writes no longer construct File(documentsDir, filename/outputFilename) directly. In current app/src/main/java/com/example/epilogue/data/repository/GhostwriterRepository.kt, downloadDigest now calls resolveDigestOutputFile at lines 543 and 570, and downloadDigestById calls it at lines 608 and 628 before writing. The helper at lines 1914-1933 rejects blank names, forward/backslash separators, '.'/'..', non-basename values, and then canonicalizes the destination and requires it to remain under the canonical Epilogue directory. A current regression test exists at app/src/test/java/com/example/epilogue/data/repository/GhostwriterRepositoryTest.kt lines 24-45 covering ../escape.epub, /tmp/escape.epub, nested paths, '.', '..', and blank filenames. I attempted the targeted Gradle test, but the read-only sandbox prevented Gradle from creating its wrapper lock file, so runtime test execution could not complete in this environment.
commands: rg -n "downloadDigest|downloadDigestById|escape|traversal|unexpected\.epub|safe basename|canonical" app/src/test app/src/androidTest app/src/main || true
